Facts: Liu Mou, general manager of a company, used opportunity at Yuan Tong Express (YTO) to steal 20167 pieces of express waybills (快递单据) from the courier company without staff knowledge. Then he organized staff to sort them, and used the personal info (including phone numbers) on the waybills to call each person to promote his company's e-commerce training services. So he stole documents containing personal data and used them for marketing.

Potential crimes: Theft (盗窃) of property (the waybills). Also possibly illegal acquisition of personal information (侵犯公民个人信息罪) under Chinese law. The act of obtaining personal information by illegal means and using it for profit may constitute "非法获取公民个人信息罪" (illegal acquisition of personal information) or "非法提供公民个人信息罪". Actually, the law on personal information: Criminal Law amendment (2015) includes article 253: "非法获取公民个人信息" (illegal acquisition of personal information) and article 254: "非法出售、提供公民个人信息". The act of stealing waybills (which contain personal info) and using them for marketing likely qualifies as illegal acquisition of personal information. Also theft of the waybills themselves is theft.

But typical Chinese criminal classification: Theft of mail (邮政管理) maybe "侵犯公民个人信息罪" is more appropriate. However the waybills are property of the courier company; stealing them is theft. The number is large (20k). So theft (盗窃) is definitely.
